title: Fabricating Cotton Analytical Devices
protocol: Determine the hydrophobicity of the exterior layer of the cleansing cotton by contact angle measurement.
Cut cleansing cotton into 5.5 cm x 1 cm pieces using a paper cutter.
Drill holes (ø = 0.5 cm) in a standard sheet of lamination film in rows of three; distance between two subsequent holes is 1 cm.
Sandwich cleansing cotton characterized by exterior hydrophobicity and interior hydrophilicity between two pieces of lamination film, one hole-drilled and the other undrilled.
Place the assembly into a laminator to package the device.
Cut individual 5.5 cm x 1 cm test strip devices from the assembly, i.e., the drilled lamination sheet/cotton pad/undrilled lamination sheet "sandwich".
Prepare 48 devices in total for creating standard curves: 18 devices for the nitrite assay, 15 devices for the BSA assay, and 15 devices for the urobilinogen assay.
Cut a slit from the center of each test area across to the hydrophilic layer using a sharp knife or razor.
Apply paper test pads (ø = 0.5 cm) by sliding them into the gaps at the perimeter of each hole in the lamination.
Prepare a 10.0 mM nitrite stock solution by dissolving 69.0 mg sodium nitrite in 100 ml deionized water.
Dilute the nitrite stock solution in DI water to create a series of nitrite concentration standard solutions (2,500, 1,250, 625, 312, 156, and 78 µM).
Dissolve 415 mg of bovine serum albumin (BSA) in 100 ml of PBS solution to prepare a 60 µM BSA stock solution.
Dilute the 60 µM BSA stock solution in DI water to create series concentrations of 30, 15, 7.5, 3.75, and 1.875 µM.
Dissolve 2.5 g of urobilinogen in 100 ml of DI water to prepare a 25 g/L stock solution.
Dilute the 25 g/L urobilinogen stock solution in DI water to create series concentrations of 7.8, 15.6, 31.2, 62.5, and 125 mg/L.
Prepare nitrite indicator solution containing 50 mM sulfanilamide, 330 mM citric acid, and 10 mM N-(1-naphthyl) ethylenediamine dihydrochloride.
Prepare BSA indicator solution containing 250 mM citrate buffer (pH 1.8) and 3.3 mM tetrabromophenol blue in 95% ethanol.
Prepare urobilinogen indicator solution containing 0.1 M 4-Dimethylamine benzaldehyde.
Cut three circular pads of diameter 0.5 cm from chromatography paper for each assay on the test strip device.
Insert the prepared pads into each lamination film hole, ensuring a slight gap between the lamination film and the cotton test pad at the edges.
Coat the nitrite assay pad with 4 µl of nitrite indicator solution and allow it to dry completely at ambient temperature.
Coat the total protein assay pad with 4 µl of BSA indicator solution and allow it to dry completely at ambient temperature.
Coat the uroblinogen assay pad with 4 µl of uroblinogen indicator and allow it to dry completely at ambient temperature.
Scan the test pads to analyze colorimetric changes occurring at each pad.
Place the resulting test pads on the glass of a desktop scanner.
Scan the test pads in RGB mode with 600 dpi image resolution.
Save each scanned image in jpeg format.
Open the scanned image files using ImageJ software.
Convert RGB images to 8-bit grayscale.
Select the analytical area of the test pad using the "Oval" tool.
Analyze color intensity by selecting “Measure” under “Analyze” menu commands.
Record mean intensity results.
Establish standard curves for nitrite, total protein, and urobilinogen assays.
Indicate different concentrations of standard solutions on a two-dimensional coordinate system.
Correlate mean intensity results with the concentrations using statistical software.
Fit the standard curve for the nitrite assay by a quadratic model.
Fit the standard curves for total protein and urobilinogen assays by linear regression models.
Determine unknown sample concentrations using established standard curve values.
Use the device as described for measuring standard solution concentrations.
Substitute measured intensity results for nitrite, total protein, and urobilinogen assays into the equations of the models built in step 2.
